solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What is neat on a river — a new boat

parts.note: something neat and tidy is trim
a stays as written and R is the standard abbreviation for river
a stays as written and N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Something tidy sits on a river, a new kind of vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing vessel with three parallel hulls, so it is a type of boat.

clue.text: Messages revealing English maiden is unwell

parts.note: M is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a maiden over, one with no runs scored
someone who ails is unwell

explanation.surface: Letters disclose that an English young woman is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored, written M on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic letters sent over the internet are a kind of message.

clue.text: Food so-so, from what's said

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word as it is spoken, so a word with the same sound but another spelling is wanted

parts.note: so-so means middling, fair

explanation.surface: A verdict that the meal is only mediocre, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is the food served at a meal, as in simple country cooking.

clue.text: Something used to fix broken plates

indicators.note: broken plates are in pieces, so the letters of the word plates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A repair tip: what you might use to mend some smashed crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire staple fastens papers or fixes material in place.

clue.text: One challenging thing weighing on other ranks, initially

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of, weighing on, the second

parts.note: an object is a thing

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the words other and ranks are taken

explanation.surface: A rebel's grievance about some burden pressing on the ordinary soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weighing on' places OBJECT above the first letters of 'other ranks' in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises an objection challenges a proposal or ruling.

clue.text: Youngster is taking time to become a Picasso

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, as in a cub scout or cub reporter

explanation.surface: A child takes the time to grow into a great artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded Cubism, so he is the classic example of a Cubist painter.

clue.text: Love some French poems

parts.note: love is a score of zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
des is French for some

explanation.surface: An admirer's collection of romantic verse written in French.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject, so several are poems.

clue.text: Violent farm animal encountering quiet little creature

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep on a farm
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
an ant is a small insect

explanation.surface: A savage beast on the farm comes across a tiny creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant violence is unrestrained and fierce, as in a rampant mob.

clue.text: Destined to make a leap

definitions.meaning: destined or certain to reach it

explanation.definitionFit: Bound means both certain to happen and to spring forward in a leap.

clue.text: State chief given a hearing

indicators.note: words that are heard rather than read point to a soundalike spelt differently

parts.note: chief means principal, main

explanation.surface: A head of state or governor is allowed to make his case.
explanation.definitionFit: Maine is a US state in New England.

clue.text: Head of Police negligent? That's the assumption

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the word Police

parts.note: remiss means careless, negligent

explanation.surface: A careless police chief? That is what people take for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiss (also premise) is a proposition assumed as the basis of an argument.

clue.text: Listener puzzles — one gets stuck in, never giving up?

indicators.note: the numeral one is inserted into the jumbled letters
puzzles as a verb means confuses, so the letters of Listener are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Solvers of the Listener, the Times' famously hard crossword, are a determined lot who never quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzles' turns LISTENER into RESLIENT, and 'gets stuck in' places I (one) after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A resilient person recovers from setbacks and keeps going, persistent rather than quitting.

clue.text: Not be able to arrange a date, alas?

parts.note: to lack something is to be without it, here unable to get it fixed up
a date on the calendar is a day

explanation.surface: A sigh of regret at failing to set up a romantic meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: To lack a day is to be unable to find a date, so the phrase falls out almost word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackaday is an old exclamation of sorrow or regret, much like alack.

clue.text: Boy for whom big book is too much

indicators.note: the full word is one letter too many, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tome is a large heavy book

explanation.surface: A lad finds a weighty volume more than he can manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is too much' says TOME has a letter to spare: drop its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom is a common short name for a boy, as in Tom Thumb.

clue.text: Controlled transport of red meats

indicators.note: transport here means to carry off or move, so the letters of red meats are shifted around

explanation.surface: Refrigerated haulage of beef and lamb was carefully regulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport of' signals an anagram of RED MEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Having mastered something means you got it under command or dominated it.

clue.text: Sleep with back of neck not completely visible

indicators.note: not completely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the nape is the back of the neck

explanation.surface: Dozing with the nape of one's neck partly hidden by a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A short doze during the day is a brief sleep.

clue.text: Work round edge in proper manner

indicators.note: round means the first word is wrapped around the second

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: An instruction to work around a border carefully and correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a verb here, as in plying a trade, not a noun for a job of work; 'round' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting primly is behaving in a starchy, prudish and correct fashion.

clue.text: Reduces legal documents

definitions.meaning: a verb: something that ... shrinks or gets smaller
a plural noun: binding written agreements

explanation.definitionFit: Contracts means shrinks as a verb and binding agreements as a noun.

clue.text: No catches in these musical pieces

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: These compositions contain no tricks or hidden snags.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition for nine instruments or voices.

clue.text: Garment a foot short kept in vessel

indicators.note: kept in means the pieces are held inside the container word

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel
ft is the short form of foot

explanation.surface: A robe that is twelve inches too short has been stored in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a foot short' looks like a garment that is too short; it is A plus the short form of foot, and 'kept in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A caftan (or kaftan) is a long loose robe or tunic.

clue.text: Country sound of composer Benjamin

indicators.note: sound of points to a word pronounced the same but spelt differently

parts.note: Benjamin Britten was the English composer of Peter Grimes

explanation.surface: A national voice heard in the music of an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is the nation formed by England, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: Group of five hundred enthralled by young male

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so one letter is held within the other word

parts.note: a boy is a young male
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A crowd of five hundred captivated by a teenage lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of people is an organised group, as in a governing body.

clue.text: Amazing affection masks this mistake

indicators.note: masks means conceals, so the answer lies inside the words Amazing affection

explanation.surface: A display of extraordinary fondness covers up an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masks' says the answer is concealed across AmazinG AFFEction.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or tactless error.

clue.text: Female US soldier joining both sides

parts.note: GI is the familiar term for an American soldier
both sides are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: A woman in the American army who joins up with both factions.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl is a young female person.

clue.text: Greek character was first on return to get word of gratitude

indicators.note: on return means the word for was first is read back to front

parts.note: to have led is to have been in front
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A Greek who led the field gets thanked when he comes back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns LED into DEL. TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Domestic row?

parts.note: row here means a line of houses rather than a quarrel at home, so this names a street of joined houses

explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic row' suggests a household quarrel, but it is a row of homes; in Britain a terrace is a line of houses built joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a continuous row of identical attached dwellings.
